findings.description: updateLocation reads result.externalId/credentialId which updateEvent never returns — The persisted booking references lose `externalCalendarId` and `credentialId`, breaking calendar targeting for reschedules and cancellations. Fall back to `evt.destinationCalendar` fields or have `CalendarManager.updateEvent` return them.

Calendar lookup by credentialId fails when destination lacks credentialId, falling back to 'primary' — Events are inserted into `'primary'` instead of the intended destination calendar when that destination has no `credentialId`. Fall back to the first destination entry's `externalId` when no `credentialId` match is found.

Dropped '|| []' guard allows null/undefined to reach users.some() at line 770 — When `eventType.users` is null, `loadUsers` resolves to `undefined` and `users.some(...)` throws before the `eventType.userId` fallback runs, turning a bookable type into a 500. Keep the `|| []` guard on the fallback.

Optional push on null destinationCalendar silently discards team calendars — For COLLECTIVE events where `evt.destinationCalendar` is null, the optional push is a no-op and no calendar events are created. Initialize the array before pushing `teamDestinationCalendars`.

Inverted slug condition drops org slug when billing is disabled — Self-hosted instances (where `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` is false) now create organizations with no slug. Restore the negated condition so the slug is set when billing is disabled.

Recurring deletion fan-out executes once per calendar reference (N× redundant API calls) — A recurring booking with N calendar references triggers N identical full delete fan-outs, multiplying API calls. Hoist the recurring-deletion block out of the per-reference loop so it runs only once.

deleteEvent fallback compares externalId to falsy value, never matches — With a falsy `externalCalendarId`, the `find` compares against `undefined` and never matches, so the delete targets `'primary'` and the real event is silently orphaned. Use the destination calendar's `externalId` as the fallback.

Fallback find compares against falsy externalCalendarId, yielding undefined calendarId — When `externalCalendarId` is falsy, the `find` compares against `undefined` and yields no match, so `calendar.events.update` receives `calendarId: undefined`. Fall back to `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId` instead.

Guest blacklist bypassed by untrimmed entries and case-sensitive guest comparison — The guest blacklist is split on ',' without .trim() and compared case-sensitively against the un-lowercased guest input: an env value like 'a@b.com, c@d.com' yields ' c@d.com' which never matches, and a guest typed as 'C@d.com' bypasses the lowercased 'c@d.com' entry. Trim each entry and lowercase guest before the includes() check so the blacklist cannot be silently defeated.

Permission check uses && instead of ||, denying ADMIN-only users access — The permission check on line 47 uses `isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner`, but `isTeamAdmin` returns a truthy object for ADMIN|OWNER while `isTeamOwner` returns a boolean that is true only for OWNER. This means ADMIN-only users (who are not OWNER) will fail the check and be incorrectly denied access.

sendAddGuestsEmails receives raw guests instead of uniqueGuests, causing wrong email type to… — sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) passes the raw input instead of uniqueGuests, so if the request resubmits an existing attendee's email (which the server permits — it only filters those out of the DB write), the newGuests.includes(attendee.email) check in sendAddGuestsEmails (email-manager.ts:541) is true for that pre-existing attendee and they receive an AttendeeScheduledEmail ('you've been scheduled' with a new REQUEST ICS) instead of the new-guests-added notice. Pass uniqueGuests.

Server schema allows duplicate guest emails, causing duplicate BookingAttendee rows — The server-side schema is z.array(z.string().email()) with no uniqueness refine — unlike the client dialog's ZAddGuestsInputSchema — so any authenticated user calling the tRPC endpoint directly with guests: ["a@x.com", "a@x.com"] passes validation and createMany (addGuests.handler.ts:101) inserts two identical BookingAttendee rows, which then each get an email and calendar invite. Enforce uniqueness server-side (refine on a Set or dedupe before the write).

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns safeParse wrapper, not parsed data — `key` receives the `{success, data, error}` wrapper instead of the parsed credential, so the next `setCredentials` call gets no top-level `access_token`. Append `.data` to the `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)` call, matching the pattern in office365calendar, salesforce, and zoomvideo.

Computed Zod keys don't create a catch-all; unknown token fields are stripped — `minimumTokenResponseSchema` relies on `[z.string().toString()]` for a passthrough, but Zod resolves that to a fixed literal key, so unknown fields like `expires_in` and `refresh_token` are silently stripped. Add `.passthrough()` to the schema instead.

Webhook secret compared with !== instead of constant-time comparison — A plain `!==` on the webhook secret leaks timing information to an attacker. Replace it with `crypto.timingSafeEqual` over equal-length buffers of the header value and `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`.
deleteMany retryCount branch not scoped to SMS method — Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` inside that OR branch so only SMS reminders are collected.

Missing index on retryCount causes full-table scan in deleteMany — Without an index on `retryCount`, each cron run scans the entire `WorkflowReminder` table, and cost grows with every booking. Add an index on `retryCount` or `[method, retryCount]` to bound it.

Unguarded prisma update in catch block can abort entire reminder loop — If the `prisma.workflowReminder.update` in the `catch` block rejects, the exception escapes and aborts the entire loop, skipping all remaining reminders. Wrap it in its own `try/catch` so a second DB failure cannot break the batch.

Backup code login bypasses password verification when dummy totpCode is sent — A dummy `totpCode` skips the password check, letting a valid backup code grant access without the correct password. Add a `verifyPassword` call inside the backup-code block before the code is accepted.

Backup code consumption is not atomic, allowing concurrent use — Two concurrent logins can read the same `backupCodes` state and both succeed, breaking the single-use guarantee. Use an optimistic-concurrency `updateMany` with the old value in the `where` clause and check `count === 1`.

XSS: unescaped request.referer in JS string literal allows script injection — A single quote in `request.referer` breaks the JS string literal, letting an attacker execute script on the Discourse origin with the visitor's session cookie. Escape the value with `j(request.referer)` in the `postMessage` call.

Anonymous cache bypasses Referer-based embed authorization — Because `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` caches the response under a key that omits `HTTP_REFERER`, a referer-less request within 60 s receives the cached page and bypasses the `ensure_embeddable` host check. Remove the `discourse_expires_in` directive from this action.

Stored XSS via unsanitized feed HTML stored as raw_html post — Because the post is stored with `cook_method: :raw_html`, unsanitized feed markup renders directly in topic views. Run the content through `Sanitize.fragment` before `TopicEmbed.import`.

Single bad feed item aborts import of all remaining items — A `NoMethodError` or `URI::InvalidURIError` on one item raises out of the loop, and with `retry: false` the entire run stops. Wrap each item in `begin/rescue` to skip failures.

Race in `TopicEmbed.import`: check-then-create on unique `embed_url` — Two concurrent `TopicEmbed.import` calls both miss the lookup and race to `create!`; the second raises an unhandled `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`, killing the caller. Rescue that exception and roll back the orphaned topic and post.

PollFeed.execute exception prevents fetch_http fallback from running — An exception in `PollFeed#poll_feed` propagates out of `perform_retrieve` before the `fetch_http` fallback runs, making on-demand retrieval fail permanently. Wrap the `execute` call in `begin/rescue` so a failed poll falls through.

SQL injection via string interpolation in migration INSERT — A single quote in the old `site_settings` value breaks the raw `execute` string, aborting the migration mid-deploy. Replace the interpolation with `connection.quote(h)` so the value is safely escaped.

NoMethodError when embed_category setting matches no category row — On most installs the join returns no row, so indexing `[0]` yields nil and the migration aborts. Guard with `.first || {'id' => nil}` so a missing `embed_category` falls back gracefully.

NoMethodError when host is nil in before_validation — Any record with a nil `host` hits `self.host.sub!` in `before_validation` and returns a 500 instead of a validation error. Guard the call with `self.host.present?` so blank input fails format validation.

update and destroy raise NoMethodError on missing record instead of 404 — A nonexistent id makes `save_host(nil)` or `host.destroy` raise `NoMethodError`, returning a 500. Add `raise Discourse::NotFound unless host` after each `.first` lookup.

4-arg self.downsize is shadowed by 3-arg version, breaking ResizeEmoji job — Because Ruby keeps only the last definition, `resize_emoji.rb` binds `opts=100` (an Integer) and the job crashes with `NoMethodError`. Delete the stale 4-argument `downsize` and update `resize_emoji.rb` to pass `"100x100"`.

Hardcoded 10MB cap overrides per-type site setting for max upload size — Sites with `max_image_size_kb` above 10240 KB now reject valid uploads the server would accept. Restore the `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` lookup for the cap.

downsize return value ignored, causing up to 5 redundant failing ImageMagick invocations — A failed ImageMagick conversion re-runs up to 5 times per oversized upload, blocking the request each time. Break out when `OptimizedImage.downsize` returns `false`.

Spec uses :put but remove_member route requires :delete, so test never hits the intended action — The verb sends the request to `add_members` (see `config/routes.rb`), so the `remove_member` guard is never exercised. Change to `xhr :delete, :remove_member`.
Negative limit/offset params cause 500 on /groups/:id/members — Negative values produce invalid SQL, turning this public endpoint into a 500. Clamp `limit` and `offset` with `[value, 0].max`.
Unbounded client-supplied limit on members endpoint — A large `limit` forces serializing the entire member list in one response. Cap it server-side to 100.

totalPages is one too high when user_count is an exact multiple of limit — When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, `totalPages` reports one extra page, leaving the next button enabled. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` instead.

Stale I18n LRU cache when SiteSetting.default_locale changes — Changing `SiteSetting.default_locale` leaves stale values in the LRU cache until the process restarts because the key in `I18n.translate` omits any site-locale component. Add the site default locale or a generation counter to that key.

I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! not called in background job locale setup — In worker processes, `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is never invoked after `I18n.locale` is set, so fallback translations silently return missing when the site locale isn't `:en`. Call it after the locale assignment in `jobs/base.rb`.

**Also found in:**
- `lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:62-65`

Stale cache entry on tagDeviceUI failure allows device-limit bypass — A stale entry in `localCache` lets a rejected device authenticate on every retry for 29 minutes, bypassing the limit. Evict the key when `CreateOrUpdateDevice` fails, or set it only after a successful write.

Non-atomic count-then-insert allows device limit to be exceeded under concurrency — Concurrent requests for new device IDs can all pass the `CountDevices` check before any row is inserted, exceeding `s.deviceLimit` by the burst size. Enforce the cap atomically, e.g. a conditional INSERT guarded by `COUNT` inside one serializable transaction.
WithDbSession retry double-prepends query to args slice — Move the `append` outside the callback, as `CreateOrUpdateDevice` already does.

Missing double-check after acquiring write lock causes serialized I/O under concurrency — Every concurrent request after the first serializes behind `entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock`, each re-reading the manifest; the Nth startup request waits ~N file-reads, and persistent load failures make every request pay that cost. Add a double-check of `entryPointAssetsCache` after acquiring the lock so only one goroutine does the I/O.

Fire-and-forget legacy writes use request ctx which is cancelled when handler returns — The parent request `ctx` is cancelled when the handler returns, capping the 10 s timeout and aborting the legacy `Create` before it completes. Derive from `context.Background()` instead; the same pattern appears in `Delete`, `Update`, and `DeleteCollection`.

Legacy DeleteCollection duration recorded with recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration — Legacy delete-collection latency lands in `grafana_dual_writer_storage_duration_seconds` rather than the legacy histogram, making it invisible in legacy dashboards. Use `d.recordLegacyDuration` instead.

Unbounded metric cardinality: object name used as 'kind' label in Delete success path — Each distinct object name spawns a new time series in `grafana_dual_writer_storage_duration_seconds`, causing unbounded cardinality growth in Prometheus. Pass `options.Kind` to match the error path and every other recording site.

Storage create failure records duration in legacy histogram instead of storage histogram — Failed unified-store creates are invisible in `grafana_dual_writer_storage_duration_seconds` because the failure path calls `d.recordLegacyDuration`. Use `d.recordStorageDuration` to match mode1/mode2.

**Also found in:**
- `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:127-131`

TotalDocs called concurrently with BuildIndex without cacheMu.RLock — The new s.search.TotalDocs() call runs immediately after the watch-event goroutine is started (lines 207-213), which can already be inside BuildIndex writing b.cache[key]; TotalDocs (bleve.go:144-154) iterates b.cache without holding cacheMu.RLock, so this is a concurrent map read/write — Go aborts the process with a fatal error. This new call site makes the unguarded TotalDocs newly reachable at every startup.

Concurrent BuildIndex for same key leaks handles and risks on-disk index corruption — Removing the function-wide cacheMu.Lock() from BuildIndex lets two goroutines build the same key concurrently, because getOrCreateIndex (search.go:292-305) is an unlocked check-then-act called concurrently from Search (search.go:148) and the handleEvent background goroutine (search.go:237). Both builds create a bleve.Index (the same on-disk directory when size > FileThreshold), but only the last b.cache[key] write wins — the other index handle is dropped without Close(), leaking file handles, allowing two writers on one on-disk index (corruption risk), and triggering a wasted full rebuild via the ListIterator with Limit 1000000000000.

useAllAlertRuleAbilities drops isFederatedRuleGroup check — Federated Mimir rules become mutable because `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` hardcodes `isFederated = false`, bypassing the old `isFederatedRuleGroup` check. Restore that guard so `RuleActionsButtons` hides Edit/Delete/Pause/Duplicate for federated groups.

Delete menu item hidden for promRule path due to stale rulerRule guard — In the new list view only `promRule` is passed, so the stale `rulerRule` guard still hides Delete even when `canDelete` is true via the `promRule` ability path. Remove the `rulerRule` check from the render condition.

RuleActionsButtons missing rule prop causes silence drawer to render nothing — The Silence item renders but opens an empty drawer because `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` reads the undefined `rule` prop via `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule`. Pass `rule` alongside `promRule` in `GrafanaRuleListItem`.

Missing key prop on GrafanaRuleListItem in rules.map — Without a `key`, React warns and can mis-associate delete-modal and silence-drawer state across rows when the list reorders. Add `key={key}` as `GrafanaRuleLoader` used.

Missing ?? [] fallback causes TypeError when groups array is empty — When `groups` is empty, `.at(0)?.rules` is `undefined` and `.map` throws a `TypeError`. Add `?? []` before `.map` as the old code did.

Client-credentials grant token encodes 'na' instead of 'cc' as grant type — `ClientCredentialsGrantType` never sets `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` on the session context, so `initToken` encodes `'na'` instead of `'cc'`, defeating the PR for the most common M2M grant. Set it on `clientSessionCtx` before generating the access token.

isAccessTokenId uses wrong substring offset and inverted grant check — `substring(3, 5)` grabs the wrong characters and the inverted check makes the grant comparison dead, so all four token-event assertions pass unconditionally. Use `substring(4, 6)` and return `true` on a match.

Multivalued-size message uses MessageFormat syntax in i18next-rendered bundle — Users see the literal tokens `{0}` and `{2,choice,...}` instead of the actual min/max, because i18next expects `{{`/`}}` interpolation in this bundle. Switch to the `{{0}}` form and drop the choice clause; that syntax belongs only in server-side FreeMarker bundles.

Listener guard checks V1 but management() dispatches on V2, causing 500 on client removal — The listener guard checks ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) while management() dispatches on ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2, and ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent is published unconditionally from JpaRealmProvider.removeClient:1006 with no exception handling in publish(). When both features are enabled, deleting any client makes the event pass the V1 guard and reach MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() -> ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled, which throws UnsupportedOperationException, aborting the client removal with a 500 (pre-PR the V2 class inherited the working V1 cleanup).

getClientsWithPermission includes resource-type resource name instead of client ID — The caller AvailableRoleMappingResource.getRoleIdsWithPermissions (line 230) iterates the set as client IDs and calls realm.getClientById(cid).getRolesStream(), which NPEs when cid='Clients'. Skip the resource-type resource (e.g. filter resources whose name equals AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) or translate a granted 'all-clients' permission into all client IDs.

Passkey form rendered on lockout/disabled error pages allows bypassing disabled state — A locked or disabled user can bypass the block via `WebAuthnAuthenticator.action`, which calls `context.success()` without re-checking `isEnabled()` or brute-force state. Gate the `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` branch so it skips rendering when the user is disabled or brute-force locked.

Unbounded searchKeys growth in login cache for multi-organization realms — In multi-organization realms, each new `organizationId` permanently appends to `IdentityProviderListQuery.searchKeys`, inflating the cached entity and forcing `invalidateObject` on every first-time lookup. Pass a fresh query instead of copying the old `query` so `searchKeys` does not accumulate across rebuilds.

TableWidgetVisualization receives hardcoded empty data instead of actual query results — Any org with the flag on sees empty grids for every table widget because the in-scope `result` data is discarded. Pass `result.data` and `result.meta` through and derive `columns` from `result.meta.fields`.

fetch_error_details pairs error_ids with nodestore results positionally via zip — Because the nodestore backend returns rows in DB order and omits missing IDs, `zip` misattributes titles and timestamps to the wrong `error_id` and silently drops trailing entries. Build a `node_id`→`event_id` map and iterate over `events.items()` instead.

Unguarded dict access on integration.metadata["sender"] causes KeyError — `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` is an unguarded double index: integrations created before this change (or via any path where state lacked "sender", as allowed by build_integration's `if state.get("sender")` at line 376 and explicitly anticipated by installation.py:44 `if "sender" not in integration.metadata`) raise KeyError → HTTP 500 on the reinstall flow instead of the intended graceful error page. Use `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")` — a missing sender then fails the equality check and fails closed.

Uncaught exception from get_user_info causes 500 on GitHub auth failure — get_user_info is called outside the try/except that only wraps the token-response read, and it internally calls resp.raise_for_status() and resp.json(). When GitHub returns a 401 (invalid/expired token) or 403/429 (rate limit), the HTTPError/decode error propagates unhandled out of the view, producing a 500 instead of the graceful error(request, self.active_organization) page this step is designed to show on verification failure.

MetricAlertDetectorHandler left abstract with unimplemented methods — `Detector.detector_handler` will raise `TypeError` on any `metric_alert_fire` detector, crashing the `process_detectors` loop and skipping the rest. Implement the abstract methods as stubs, or stop wiring the class as `MetricAlertFire.detector_handler` until it's concrete.
